policies.title: Colombia: citizenship treatment
policies.summary: A Colombian citizen returns under Colombian citizenship and national-document rules rather than the foreign visitor-visa framework.
conditions: Colombian citizens have the right to enter and must identify themselves as Colombian when they also hold another nationality.
Check-Mig is optional and recommended; it is not an ETA or entry authorization.
Does not determine dual-national documentation, passport validity, minors' exit consent or case-specific border circumstances.

policies.title: Colombia: list A ordinary passports are visa-free for qualifying short stays
policies.summary: The current amended list A exempts these ordinary-passport nationalities from a visa for qualifying short non-remunerated visits.
conditions: Short stays cover qualifying non-remunerated activities such as tourism, leisure, business, events or cultural interest; paid services, salary or wages in Colombia require a visa with the appropriate permission.
The normal short-stay period is less than 90 days and may be extendable up to 180 days when the applicable rules permit it.
Admission remains discretionary and subject to a valid travel document, onward travel, funds, purpose, immigration control and any health, security or individual-admissibility requirements.
Does not classify transit, work, study, residence, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, emergency, laissez-passer, national-identity-card or other special-document routes.

policies.title: Colombia: HKSAR passport short-stay exemption
policies.summary: The current list B exempts a Hong Kong Special Administrative Region passport from a visa for qualifying short non-remunerated visits.
conditions: Applies to the HKSAR passport entry in list B, not every document associated with Hong Kong or the People's Republic of China.

policies.title: Colombia: electronic visitor visa unless conditional exemption is met
policies.summary: These ordinary-passport nationalities need Colombia's electronic Visitor visa unless they meet the official third-country residence or visa condition for short-stay exemption.
conditions: Visa-free entry may be authorized with a valid residence permit from a Schengen state or the United States, or a Schengen or United States visa valid for at least 180 days at entry.
Qualifying Nicaraguan natives of the North or South Caribbean Coast Autonomous Regions have an additional conditional short-stay exemption.
Without the stated evidence, nationality alone does not establish visa-free admission, so the baseline remains electronic visa.
The Foreign Ministry normally processes and issues the visa electronically, but may require a printed passport label when it considers that necessary.

application.label: Apply through Colombia's official SITAC electronic visa service
application.processingTime: The Foreign Ministry allows up to 30 calendar days for a decision after a complete application and study-fee payment; external consultations can take longer.
steps: Confirm that the planned activity requires a Visitor visa and choose the Colombian consular office responsible for the applicant's place of legal residence.
Complete the official online form, upload the required passport page, photograph and supporting documents, and pay the study fee.
Respond to any request through SITAC and, if approved, pay the issuance fee within the stated deadline.
Receive the electronic visa at the registered email address and travel with the same passport; a visa permits travel to request entry but does not guarantee admission.

policies.title: Colombia: other ordinary passports require an electronic Visitor visa
policies.summary: Ordinary-passport nationalities outside the current unconditional and conditional short-stay exemptions must obtain Colombia's electronic Visitor visa before travel.
conditions: A separate visa-free exception may apply to a qualifying permanent resident of a Pacific Alliance or Andean Community state, or under a current bilateral agreement; nationality alone does not establish those status-based routes.

The Foreign Ministry conducts study, processing and issuance virtually and sends the approved electronic visa to the registered email address; it may require original documents, an interview or, when it considers necessary, a printed passport label.
